bull.t: Large backlog and recurring aftermarket revenue
bull.b: RTX combines a record multiyear backlog with a large installed base that generates recurring maintenance, spares and sustainment revenue. This improves revenue visibility and reduces dependence on new equipment deliveries over the next several years.

bull.t: Raised growth, margin and cash outlook
bull.b: Higher guidance across sales, earnings and free cash flow indicates broad-based operating improvement rather than reliance on one program. Upgraded segment outlooks also support sustained revenue growth and margin recovery over the medium term.

bull.t: Pratt operational recovery strengthens lifecycle economics
bull.b: Improved Pratt MRO throughput and aircraft availability can restore customer confidence while expanding higher-value aftermarket capacity. The GTF Advantage certification and deliveries add a newer platform to the engine lifecycle opportunity.

bear.b: Debt reduction is encouraging, but RTX still carries meaningful leverage relative to a low-debt peer. If aerospace execution weakens or major program charges return, debt service and balance-sheet commitments could constrain investment flexibility.

bear.t: Limited gross-margin cushion and cost pressure
bear.b: A roughly 20% gross margin leaves less protection against labor, material, tariff and supply-chain inflation. Continued SG&A and tariff pressure could limit incremental profit conversion even if revenue growth remains strong.

bear.t: Pratt OE weakness and working-capital demands
bear.b: Lower commercial original-equipment sales and mix shifts can slow near-term Pratt revenue growth while production scales. Inventory investment and working-capital absorption may also make cash generation less predictable during the ramp.
